recipes.name: Vanilla Birthday Layer Cake
recipes.summary: A tender, buttery two-layer vanilla cake, the classic birthday cake. Frost it with vanilla or chocolate buttercream.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Grease the pans, line the bottoms with parchment circles, and grease the parchment. Flour the sides lightly, tapping out the extra.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar on medium-high speed for 3 to 4 minutes, until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

On low speed, add the flour mixture in three parts and the milk in two, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until no flour shows. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Divide the batter between the pans and smooth the tops. Bake 28 to 32 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn the layers out onto racks, peel off the parchment and cool completely, about 1 hour, before frosting.
To frost, see “Frost a layer cake” on the Birthday parties page: a thin crumb coat, 20 minutes in the refrigerator, then the final coat.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake the layers up to 2 days ahead, cool, wrap tightly and keep at room temperature, or freeze them. Frost the day before or the morning of the party.

freezer.text: Wrap cooled layers in plastic wrap and foil and freeze up to 2 months. Frost them while still a little frozen; they crumb less.

leftovers.text: Keep a buttercream-frosted cake covered at room temperature up to 2 days, or refrigerated up to 5.

recipes.kids: Kids can measure, crack eggs into a separate bowl, and run the mixer on low with a grown-up.

swaps.cupcakes: This batter makes about 30 cupcakes; bake 18 to 20 minutes.
swaps.sheet: Bake it in a 9-by-13-inch pan for 35 to 40 minutes.
swaps.gluten_free: A cup-for-cup gluten-free flour blend that contains xanthan gum works in this cake.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the layers up to 2 days before.

recipes.name: Chocolate Birthday Layer Cake
recipes.summary: A dark, moist one-bowl chocolate cake made with cocoa, oil and hot water. No mixer needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the pans, line the bottoms with parchment circles, and grease the parchment. Flour the sides lightly, tapping out the extra.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt in a large bowl until no lumps of cocoa remain.
Add the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla and whisk 2 minutes, until smooth.

A grown-up pours in the boiling water while whisking slowly. The batter will be thin; that’s right. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Pour into the pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter.
Cool 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto racks and cool completely before frosting.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 2 days ahead, wrap well and keep at room temperature, or freeze.

freezer.text: Wrap cooled layers in plastic wrap and foil; freeze up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Keep covered at room temperature up to 2 days, or refrigerated up to 5.

recipes.kids: Kids can whisk the dry ingredients. A grown-up adds the boiling water.

swaps.deeper_flavor: Use hot coffee instead of boiling water.
swaps.dairy_free: Use any plant milk with 1 tablespoon vinegar stirred in.
swaps.cupcakes: Makes about 30 cupcakes; bake 18 to 22 minutes.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the layers up to 2 days before.

recipes.name: Vanilla Sheet Cake for a Crowd
recipes.summary: One big, flat vanilla cake for a class or a crowd. Frost it right in the pan; no stacking or leveling.
equipment: half-sheet pan (13 by 18 inches, 1 inch deep)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the half-sheet pan, line it with parchment, and grease the parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar 4 minutes, until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

On low speed, add the flour in three parts and the milk in two, mixing just until smooth. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Spread the batter evenly in the pan. Bake 28 to 32 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool completely in the pan on a rack. Frost the top with 1½ batches of buttercream and cut 4 by 6 for 24 squares (or 6 by 8 for 48 small ones).
recipes.make_ahead: Bake a day ahead and keep it covered at room temperature; frost that evening or the morning of the party.

freezer.text: Freeze the unfrosted cake, wrapped well in the pan, up to 1 month.

leftovers.text: Keep covered at room temperature up to 2 days, or refrigerated up to 5.

recipes.kids: Kids can decorate the frosted top with sprinkles, fruit or a candy border.

swaps.smaller: Halve everything and bake in a 9-by-13-inch pan for 30 to 35 minutes.

credits.name: Flour, Raw Food and Other Safety Facts (FDA)

recipes.name: Chocolate Sheet Cake with Fudge Frosting
recipes.summary: A thin, fudgy chocolate cake in a half-sheet pan, with a glossy cocoa frosting poured over while it’s warm. Feeds a crowd, ready in about an hour.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease the half-sheet pan.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In a saucepan, bring the butter, cocoa and water to a boil, stirring. Pour it over the flour mixture and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Pour into the pan and spread it to the corners. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.

About 5 minutes before the cake is done, make the frosting: melt the butter with the cocoa and milk in a saucepan, bring just to a simmer, take it off the heat and whisk in the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the warm frosting over the hot cake and spread it quickly; it sets as it cools. Cool at least 30 minutes before cutting into 24 squares.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake the day before; keep it covered at room temperature.

freezer.text: Freeze squares between layers of parchment up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Keep covered at room temperature up to 3 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can whisk the dry ingredients and help pour the cooler parts. A grown-up handles the boiling butter and the hot frosting.

swaps.nuts: Many families scatter chopped pecans over the frosting; leave them off for a nut-free party.
swaps.buttermilk: Use ½ cup milk with 1½ teaspoons vinegar stirred in.

recipes.name: Vanilla Cupcakes
recipes.summary: Soft vanilla cupcakes, 24 to a batch. Easy to carry to school, easy to hand out, no slicing.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line 24 muffin cups.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar 3 minutes until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

On low, mix in the flour in three parts and the milk in two, just until smooth. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Fill the liners two-thirds full (a scant ¼ cup each). Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes in the pans, then on racks. Frost when completely cool: swirl on buttercream with a knife, or pipe it from a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake a day ahead and keep in a covered container; frost the day of the party.

freezer.text: Freeze unfrosted cupcakes in a bag up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature in their bag.

leftovers.text: Keep covered at room temperature up to 2 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can fill the liners with a scoop and decorate the frosted tops.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a cup-for-cup gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant-based butter stick and plant milk; check the butter label for milk.

recipes.name: Chocolate Cupcakes
recipes.summary: Moist one-bowl chocolate cupcakes made with cocoa and oil. They stay soft for days.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line 24 muffin cups.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt.

Whisk in the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla until smooth. A grown-up whisks in the boiling water; the batter will be thin. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Fill the liners about half full (a pitcher or measuring cup makes it easy). Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely before frosting.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake a day ahead; frost the day of the party.

leftovers.text: Keep covered at room temperature up to 3 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can line the pans and whisk the dry ingredients.

recipes.name: Egg-Free, Dairy-Free Chocolate Cake (Wacky Cake)
recipes.summary: The old “wacky cake”: no eggs, milk or butter, mixed right in the pan, risen with baking soda and vinegar. Handy when a guest can’t have eggs or dairy.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. You don’t need to grease the pan.
Stir the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt together right in the pan with a fork, and smooth it out.
Poke three wells in the dry mixture: a big one, a medium one and a small one. Pour the oil into the big one, the vinegar into the medium one and the vanilla into the small one.

Pour the water over everything and stir with the fork until no dry spots remain, getting into the corners. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pan.
Dust with powdered sugar, or frost with a dairy-free buttercream (see the swaps).
recipes.make_ahead: Bake a day ahead; keep covered at room temperature.

leftovers.text: Keep covered at room temperature up to 3 days.

recipes.kids: A great first cake: kids can do every step but the oven, and it’s fun to watch the vinegar fizz.

swaps.frosting: For a dairy-free frosting, make the vanilla buttercream with vegetable shortening or a plant-based butter stick and plant milk. Check every label for milk.
swaps.cupcakes: Doubled, it makes about 20 cupcakes; bake 18 to 20 minutes.
swaps.gluten_free: Use a cup-for-cup gluten-free flour blend.

recipes.name: Vanilla Buttercream
recipes.summary: Fluffy American buttercream: butter beaten with powdered sugar, cream and vanilla. Enough to fill and frost a two-layer cake or 24 cupcakes.
steps: Beat the butter on medium-high for 3 minutes, until pale and creamy.
On low speed, add the powdered sugar a cup at a time. Add the cream, vanilla and salt.
Beat on medium-high 2 to 3 minutes, until light and fluffy. Add a spoonful more cream if it’s too stiff, or more sugar if too soft.
To tint it, stir in food coloring a drop at a time; gel colors give stronger color with less liquid.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 week in the refrigerator. Let it soften on the counter and beat it again before using.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months; thaw in the refrigerator and re-beat.

recipes.kids: Kids can add the sugar on low speed (with a towel over the bowl to stop the cloud) and choose the colors.

swaps.dairy_free: Use vegetable shortening or a plant-based butter stick and plant milk; check labels for milk.

prep_day.ahead: Make up to a week ahead and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Chocolate Buttercream
recipes.summary: Creamy cocoa buttercream for filling and frosting a two-layer cake or 24 cupcakes.
steps: Beat the butter on medium-high for 3 minutes, until creamy.
On low speed, add the powdered sugar and cocoa alternately with the cream, a little at a time.
Add the vanilla and salt and beat on medium-high 2 to 3 minutes, until fluffy. Adjust with a spoonful of cream or sugar.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 week in the refrigerator; soften and re-beat before using.
recipes.kids: Kids can sift the cocoa and sugar.

swaps.dairy_free: Use shortening or a plant-based butter stick and plant milk; check labels for milk.

prep_day.ahead: Make up to a week ahead and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
recipes.summary: Tangy, smooth frosting for chocolate, vanilla or carrot cake. A cake frosted with it lives in the refrigerator.
steps: Beat the cream cheese and butter together until smooth, about 2 minutes. Both should be soft, or you’ll get lumps.
On low speed, beat in the powdered sugar a cup at a time, then the vanilla and salt. Beat just until creamy; overbeating makes it runny.
Chill 15 minutes if it’s too soft to spread.
Keep a cake or cupcakes with this frosting in the refrigerator, and set it out for the party for no more than 2 hours (USDA).

freezer.text: Freeze up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator and stir.

recipes.kids: Kids can add the sugar on low speed.

recipes.name: Hot Fudge Sauce (and a Sundae Bar)
recipes.summary: Thick, glossy chocolate sauce in 10 minutes, for an ice cream sundae bar at the party or a scoop next to the cake.
steps: Whisk the cream, corn syrup, brown sugar, cocoa and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a simmer, whisking, and simmer 1 minute.
Take it off the heat. Add the chocolate chips and butter, wait 1 minute, then whisk until smooth. Stir in the vanilla.
Serve warm. A grown-up should check that it’s warm, not hot, before kids spoon it on.
For a sundae bar, set out scoops of ice cream in cups just before serving, with the fudge, berries, sliced bananas, sprinkles and whipped cream. Put the ice cream back in the freezer between rounds.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 weeks in a jar in the refrigerator. Rewarm in short bursts in the microwave, stirring.
recipes.kids: Kids can set up the topping bowls.

swaps.dairy_free: Use full-fat coconut milk, coconut oil and dairy-free chips.

recipes.name: Make-Your-Own Mini Pizzas
recipes.summary: English muffin halves the guests top themselves with sauce, cheese and toppings. A party activity and lunch in one.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. If you like a crisper base, toast the muffin halves on the sheets for 4 minutes first.

Set out the muffin halves, sauce, cheese and toppings in bowls. Each guest spreads a spoonful of sauce, sprinkles cheese and adds toppings. Write names on the parchment with a pencil so everyone gets their own.
A grown-up bakes them 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese melts and bubbles.
Cool 3 minutes; melted cheese is very hot. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Dice toppings the day before. Assemble and bake at the party.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: The guests make these themselves; a grown-up handles the oven.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free English muffins or bagels.
swaps.from_scratch: Use the from-scratch pizza dough, rolled into 4-inch rounds; bake 10 to 12 minutes.

recipes.name: Party Pigs in a Blanket
recipes.summary: Little pieces of hot dog wrapped in biscuit dough and baked golden. The snack that disappears first.

ingredients.prep: refrigerated biscuits, each cut in 3 strips

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Cut each biscuit into 3 strips and stretch each strip a little. Wrap one around each piece of hot dog, pinching the end underneath.
Set them seam side down on the sheet and brush with egg if you like.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden. The hot dogs should be steaming hot, 165°F (USDA).

Cool 5 minutes. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA). For guests under 4, cut them into small pieces; hot dogs are a choking hazard for young children (CDC).
recipes.make_ahead: Wrap them up to 2 hours ahead and refrigerate on the sheet; bake when guests arrive.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked on a tray, then bag; bake from frozen, adding 3 to 5 minutes.

recipes.kids: Kids can wrap the dough around the hot dogs and wash their hands after.

swaps.puff_pastry: Use a sheet of thawed puff pastry cut in strips; bake at 400°F.
swaps.from_scratch: Use a half batch of from-scratch biscuit dough.

prep_day.ahead: Wrap them up to 2 hours before.

recipes.name: Crispy Baked Chicken Tenders
recipes.summary: Chicken tenders coated in Parmesan panko and baked until crunchy. Everyone’s party favorite, without frying.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set a rack on each baking sheet if you have them and brush with oil.
Set out three dishes: flour with half the salt; eggs beaten with a spoonful of water; panko mixed with the Parmesan, garlic powder, paprika, the rest of the salt and the oil.
Pat the chicken dry. Dip each tender in flour, then egg, then press it into the crumbs. Lay them on the racks. Wash your hands, and anything raw chicken touched.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and a food thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest tender (USDA).
Serve with ranch, ketchup or honey mustard. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Bread them a few hours ahead and refrigerate on the racks; bake when guests arrive.

freezer.text: Freeze baked tenders up to 3 months; reheat at 400°F to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Older kids can do the dipping, with hand-washing after.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free flour and crushed corn flakes.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the Parmesan and add ½ teaspoon more salt.

prep_day.ahead: Bread them a few hours ahead.

recipes.name: Baked Ham and Cheese Party Sliders
recipes.summary: A whole tray of soft sweet rolls filled with ham and Swiss, brushed with butter and mustard and baked until melty.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Without pulling the rolls apart, slice the whole slab in half horizontally with a serrated knife. Set the bottom in the baking dish.
Layer the ham and cheese over the bottom, then put the top back on.
Stir the butter, mustard and onion powder together and brush it over the tops.
Cover with foil and bake 15 minutes, then uncover and bake 5 minutes more, until the cheese melts and the centers are hot.
Cut into 12 sliders. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate; brush with butter and bake just before the party, adding 5 minutes.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can layer the ham and cheese.

swaps.mustard: Leave out the mustard for picky eaters.

recipes.name: Veggie Cups with Ranch Dip
recipes.summary: Each guest gets a cup with ranch in the bottom and vegetable sticks standing up in it. No double-dipping, and it looks bright on the table.
steps: Cut the celery, cucumber and pepper into sticks about 4 inches long, so they stand up above the rim.
Spoon 2 tablespoons of ranch into the bottom of each cup.
Stand 4 carrots and a few sticks of each vegetable in each cup.
Keep the cups in the refrigerator until serving, then set them out on a tray of ice. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables a day ahead and store them in containers with a damp paper towel. Fill the cups up to 3 hours ahead and refrigerate.

freezer.text: Raw vegetables don’t freeze for this.

swaps.hummus: Use hummus in some cups for guests who can’t have milk or eggs (it contains sesame).
swaps.from_scratch: Make the ranch dressing from scratch.

recipes.name: Fresh-Squeezed Party Lemonade
recipes.summary: Real lemonade from fresh lemons and a simple syrup, a gallon pitcher for the party. Not too sweet; add more syrup to taste.
steps: Make a syrup: heat the sugar with 1 cup of the water, stirring, until it dissolves. Let it cool.
Squeeze the lemons and strain out the seeds.
In a pitcher, stir the lemon juice, syrup and the remaining 6 cups of cold water. Taste and add a little more water or sugar.
Chill, and serve over ice with lemon slices.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the syrup and juice up to 3 days ahead and keep them in the refrigerator; mix with water the day of the party.

freezer.text: Freeze in ice cube trays to cool the pitcher without watering it down.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the lemons on the counter to loosen the juice and help squeeze them.

swaps.pink: Stir in ½ cup of strawberry purée.
swaps.sparkling: Use sparkling water for half of the water.

prep_day.ahead: Squeeze the lemons and make the syrup.
